prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind O&M; scope to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere); excludes public grid, non-farm port ops. Wildmere: boundary/dispatch/status; Export Limit Advisory when capability<target; applies accepted ceiling, records time. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): validated commands within protections, blocks conflicts, safe mode on auxiliary loss; Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor feed Turbine Sensor Bus. Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur): Leading Edge Tile Image, repeat pass if coverage low; Blade Specialist reviews. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer (limits), export cable, Export Cable Monitor, station service transformers, Fire Detection Panel; Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room; mode Substation Degraded. Substation Operator: approved switching, clearances, escalates alarms, notifies Grid Dispatcher. Electrical Technician under isolation. Emergency Generator (Foxglove): auto-start on auxiliary loss, no unapproved paralleling, sheds loads; Start Test Trace; failure→defect. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): time-stamped data→Shore Control Room (Amber Quay); Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway; records security access/control events. Shore Control Room: dispatch target/ramp, keeps last validated limit on grid comms loss; operational view, coordinates protective actions. Grid Dispatcher: targets; priority safety>protection>export. Control Engineer validates, records deviations. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard): Position Quality Flag. Mode Grid Constraint. Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown): Squall Window Bulletin, Deferred Task Rationale. Duty Planner: mobilization (CTV/Daughter Craft/SOV/Helideck); Transfer Manifest Addendum→Vessel Master. Crew Transfer Vessel: Harness Audit Card. Weather Analyst: Wave Burst Record. Port Agent: Berth Slot Confirmation. Redoubt (permit control) blocks release. Vessel Master: reconciles headcount before underway, Crew Count Correction on mismatch, records transit crew changes, onboard count. Personnel Tracking Console; North/South Access Scanner. Accountability before vessel-to-structure transfer, at disembark vs return roster; records time/location/role/disposition; comms loss→local record. Field Supervisor confirms party complete, escalates absences→Marine Coordinator (transit, return movements). HSE Officer scheduled checks. Cybersecurity Gateway monitors external traffic; Cybersecurity Analyst reviews alerts, escalates to on-duty operations lead; continuous monitoring. Control/SCADA Engineer individual

New part:
S428: Cybersecurity Analyst produces the Firmware Hash Attestation for controlled software releases.
S429: Field Supervisor checks that cybersecurity requirements are included in the work briefing before technicians begin affected tasks.
S430: Field Supervisor uses the Deferred Task Rationale when a cybersecurity-related work item must be postponed.
S431: Personnel report suspected compromise, lost credentials, and unexplained equipment behavior promptly through the established operations channel.
S432: The incident lead classifies each report, assigns an owner, and records its time, scope, and current status.
S433: When containment is needed, technical teams isolate only the affected connection or service where this can be done without creating an unsafe operating condition.
S434: The Control Engineer and Electrical Technician coordinate any operational changes with the relevant duty role before implementation.
S435: The Cybersecurity Analyst preserves relevant logs and technical evidence while limiting access to personnel assigned to the investigation.
S436: Recovery begins only after the incident lead confirms that the threat is contained and the affected system is suitable for return to service.
S437: The SCADA Engineer validates restored configurations and communications before normal monitoring responsibilities resume.
S438: Material actions and decisions are documented with the time, location, responsible role, and disposition.
S439: After significant incidents, the technical teams review causes, response effectiveness, and corrective actions with operations management.
S440: Blade inspection is initiated when scheduled surveillance, turbine alarms, or operational reports indicate that blade condition requires review.
S441: The Maintenance Planning Engine combines inspection intervals, prior defect history, and turbine availability to propose survey dates.
S442: The Duty Planner confirms the inspection priority and coordinates access with the Marine Coordinator or the Field Supervisor.
S443: The Weather Service and Metocean Buoy provide forecasts and measured conditions for assessing whether remote or close-access work is safe.
S444: Remote surveys use the Blade Inspection Drone to capture repeatable views of blade surfaces while the turbine is in an approved operating state.
S445: The Blade Specialist reviews the tile image to classify visible damage and identify areas requiring closer assessment.
S446: Image records are linked to the turbine, blade, inspection date, viewing angle, and relevant operating conditions.
S447: The SCADA Gateway provides operating data that helps distinguish persistent defects from transient changes in blade appearance.
S448: The Shore Control Room monitors turbine status and records any operating restrictions required during the remote survey.
S449: A remote finding that is uncertain, growing, or potentially safety significant is referred for close-access inspection.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
